Smoke Detector Guide
Before your final inspection

Smoke Detector Requirements,
Made Simple

A municipal inspector will visit before we close out your project. Take five minutes with this guide — it covers everything they'll check.

10-year sealed battery

Every alarm must carry a 10-year battery warranty — sealed, tamper-proof, no annual swaps.

Interconnected alarms

When one alarm detects smoke, every alarm in the home sounds. Hard-wired or wireless mesh both qualify.

Full coverage

A smoke detector is required in every bedroom and in the hallways leading to the sleeping areas.

See following page for enlarged image

Smoke Detector Installation Guidelines

A

Blue Markings — Inside Every Bedroom

  • Install one smoke detector in every bedroom.
  • Mount the smoke detector on the ceiling.
  • Maintain at least 3 ft of clearance from supply air vents and ceiling fans.
B

Green and Orange Markings — Hallways Outside the Bedrooms

  • Install smoke detectors in the hallways serving the sleeping areas.
  • Smoke detectors should be installed no more than 10 ft from each bedroom door.
  • Do not install a smoke detector directly outside a bathroom.
  • Maintain a minimum clearance of 3 ft between any bathroom door and a smoke detector installed in the hallway.
C

General Layout Requirements

Smoke detectors are only required inside bedrooms and in the hallways serving those bedrooms. For example, if the house has two stories:

  • If there is a bedroom on the first floor, install one smoke detector inside that bedroom and another in the hallway serving that bedroom.
  • Repeat the same layout for all bedrooms and hallways on the second floor.
Homeowner responsibilityMeeting these standards is the homeowner's responsibility — doing so before inspection day avoids repeat visits.

Terra Energy · Texas Heat Detector Guide

Where to buy compliant detectors

Quick links to detectors that meet the requirements in this guide.

🌡️

Hardwired Heat Alarm with Battery Backup

First Alert BRK HD6135FB — 135°F fixed-temperature and rate-of-rise sensing, 120V AC hardwired with 9V battery backup, UL 539 listed. Suitable for the garage heat detector location alongside the ESS battery.

View product
🔔

First Alert 9120B — Hardwired Interconnected Smoke Alarm (6-Pack)

Hardwired 120V AC smoke alarm with 9V battery backup, interconnects with up to 12 other First Alert/BRK hardwired alarms — including the heat detector above — so if either detects an emergency, all alarms sound. UL 217 listed.

View product

Both detectors listed above are compatible with each other and are designed to be interconnected, so that either one triggers the full alarm system. If you already have a smoke detector installed in your home, you (the homeowner) are solely responsible for selecting a heat detector that is compatible with your existing smoke detector and can be properly interconnected to it — Terra will help identify whether your current smoke detector system allows interconnection and which heat detector can be interconnected with it. If you do not yet have a smoke detector or a heat detector installed, you must purchase both products listed above, as they are matched to interconnect with each other.

Links are provided for convenience, not as an endorsement — always confirm the unit meets your local code before installing.

Heat Detector Guide
Before your final inspection

Heat Detector Requirements,
Made Simple

Texas follows the International Residential Code (IRC) baseline for garage fire detection. Here's what you need to know before your municipal inspection.

Homeowner installs the heat detector. The homeowner is responsible for mounting the heat detector on the ceiling, in the same room as the ESS battery (such as the garage or utility room). There is no exact required distance between the heat detector and the battery — for a standard-sized room, placing the detector in the middle of the ceiling is usually ideal, though it performs best when mounted closer to the battery system. This installation must follow this guide, local rules, and applicable code requirements, and is not performed by Terra Energy.

The exact location of your heat detector will be provided once your project's plans have been approved.

Sample garage layout showing heat detector placement relative to the ESS battery and bollards. Verify final placement per local regulations.
Alternate layout: ESS/IQ battery and heat detector mounted on the side wall nearest the garage door. No bollard is shown in this configuration — verify vehicle impact protection requirements for your specific site.
Buying the detectorAny wired or wireless heat detector works, as long as it's compatible with your home's existing smoke detector interconnection.
InstallationThe heat detector installation is the homeowner's responsibility, not Terra Energy's. Once the ESS/battery installation is complete, the homeowner is solely responsible for installing the heat detector.
Homeowner responsibilityMeeting these standards is the homeowner's responsibility — doing so before inspection day avoids repeat visits.
